claims.quote: You must get a fit note (also known as a ‘sick note’) if your health condition or disability affects your capability to work for longer than 7 days.
claims.note: The page says you must get a fit note if your condition affects your capability to work for longer than 7 days.

claims.claim: The fit note can come from a GP.
claims.quote: GP or hospital doctor registered nurse
claims.note: A GP is one of the healthcare professionals the page lists as able to give a fit note.

claims.claim: The fit note is form SC1 or an equivalent.
claims.note: The sources never mention form SC1.

claims.claim: You complete a health questionnaire for the Work Capability Assessment.
claims.quote: Before your assessment, you’ll need to complete a ‘Capability for Work’ (WCA50) health questionnaire.
claims.note: The page says you must complete a health questionnaire before your assessment.

claims.quote: Before your assessment, you’ll need to complete a ‘Capability for Work’ (WCA50) health questionnaire.
claims.note: The page names the questionnaire WCA50, not UC50.

claims.claim: You can provide medical evidence for the Work Capability Assessment.
claims.quote: You’ll be able to send copies of other medical information with this, such as treatment plans or test results.
claims.note: The page says you can send copies of other medical information with the questionnaire.

claims.claim: You may have an assessment appointment (Work Capability Assessment).
claims.quote: The assessment can be in person, by video call or on the phone.
claims.note: The page describes the Work Capability Assessment and how it can take place.

claims.claim: The assessment is with a health professional.
claims.quote: contact your health assessment provider using the details in your invitation letter
